title: model-loading-shard-download-breadcrumbs-ethan-park
content:
Goal: quick breadcrumbs for the sharded weights download + load failure seen on dedicated nodes (nodegroup-prod-02).

Symptoms observed:
- Model fails to initialize during load step: hangs for ~30s then raises 'RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading checkpoint shard' (trace below).
- Issue reproducible when fetching shards from s3://redwood-models/llama-30b-sharded/ on certain hosts, not others.
- Checksums (md5) for some shard files differ from values in manifest.json.

Commands I ran (chronological):
1) List remote files & manifest:
   aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models/llama-30b-sharded/ --recursive
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/llama-30b-sharded/manifest.json ./manifest.json

2) Download single shard (to test integrity):
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/llama-30b-sharded/shard-00012.bin ./shard-00012.bin --no-progress
   sha256sum shard-00012.bin  # local checksum

3) Attempted parallel/rsync style pull (failed mid-transfer on nodegroup-prod-02):
   aws s3 sync s3://redwood-models/llama-30b-sharded/ /mnt/checkpoints/llama-30b/ --size-only --delete

4) Tried using 's5cmd' (faster parallel):
   s5cmd --endpoint https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com cp s3://redwood-models/llama-30b-sharded/* /mnt/checkpoints/llama-30b/

Error snippets (from runtime logs):
- Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "loader.py", line 214, in load_sharded_checkpoint
      shard = torch.load(f)
  EOFError: Ran out of input

- RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading checkpoint shard (shard-00012.bin)

Observations / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: partial downloads due to transient S3 connectivity or aggressive TCP timeouts on affected hosts. Some shards show size smaller than expected (manifest lists ~2.1GB, downloaded file 1.6GB).
- Hypothesis B: disk or volume mount on nodegroup-prod-02 has IO errors causing truncation during write. Check dmesg for ext4/xfs errors.
- Hypothesis C: s3 multipart uploads for that model were corrupted at source (bad manifest). Need to verify original build pipeline that uploaded shards.
- Hypothesis D: aggressive parallel fetch (s5cmd) + limited disk bandwidth leading to corrupted writes.

Checks performed so far:
- Re-downloaded single failing shard on a healthy laptop; checksum matches manifest (so remote object is OK for that copy).
- On nodegroup-prod-02 repeated aws s3 cp gives inconsistent sizes (intermittent).
- Checked /var/log/messages and dmesg for I/O errors: found occasional "blk_update_request: I/O error" on device /dev/nvme1n1 around the time of failed downloads.
- Re-ran md5 checks against manifest.json on another working host (node-dev-03) — all good.

Immediate mitigation steps tried:
- Rebooted nodegroup-prod-02 (successfully brought it back up) — after reboot, downloads succeeded for a while, then started failing again. Points more to flaky hardware or network.
- Switched downloads to use our internal caching proxy (s3proxy) on nodegroup-prod-02 to see if chunking behavior changes; fewer failures but still one truncated file.
- Changed aws cli --no-verify-ssl and retried (no effect).

Next recommended actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run full SMART and nvme health check on /dev/nvme1n1 (smartctl / nvme-cli) to confirm drive health.
- [ ] Temporarily cordon the nodegroup-prod-02 hosts from model-loading pool until we root cause.
- [ ] Re-upload shard set from build artifacts bucket and compare ETag/md5 with manifest (ensure multipart upload integrity). In case upload was corrupted, re-publish and add end-to-end checksum job in CI.
- [ ] Add a small wrapper to loader that validates file sizes and checksums before torch.load to give clearer error & auto-retry with backoff.
- [ ] Instrument download code path to log byte counts and write success/failure at OS level.

Notes for postmortem:
- Timeline of failures suggests correlation with heavy network egress from cluster (around 10:42-11:12 UTC) — check k8s metrics and cloud network egress logs.
- Consider moving large model artifacts to a region-local, higher-availability store for Dedicated customers to avoid cross-AZ transfer issues.

Quick reproduction steps (to share with SRE):
1) On affected host, run: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/llama-30b-sharded/shard-00012.bin /tmp/shard-00012.bin && sha256sum /tmp/shard-00012.bin
2) If size mismatch or EOF during write, run: dmesg | tail -n 200 and paste logs.

Notes-to-self: file-level verification should be added to the download workflow (manifest + per-shard checksum). Also add a job that periodically verifies model bucket integrity against canonical manifest.

Links: JIRA INF-4127 (incident), PR #987 has early loader improvements (instrumentation), Confluence notes for manual restore.

--- end of scratchpad ---
